newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 25.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Rep. Han Lee-hun, former senior presidential secretary for economic affairs, admitted during a parliamentary hearing that he made a phone call to a Hanbo Group creditor bank to extend preferential loans, but denied he put any pressure on the bank.
- The government plans to permit South Koreans to travel freely to the Rajin-Sunbong free-trade zone in North Korea in the later half of this year.
- The Finance Ministry said it would take measures to lower interest rates to between six and seven percent in the mid to long term.
- President Kim Young-sam's second son Hyun-chul will testify at a parliamentary hearing on the Hanbo loans scandal on Friday.

- The South Korean Red Cross rejected its North Korean counterpart's proposal to hold a Red Cross meeting in Beijing on May 3, insisting that there is no reason to hold the meeting in a third country. Instead the head of the South Korean Red Cross proposed a working level meeting at the boarder village.
- The government rejected the new proposal by North Korea for three-way talks saying it is aimed at extracting major concessions from South Korea and the United States.
